claim:
Let \(ABC\) be an acute Euclidean triangle with side lengths \(a=BC\), \(b=CA\), \(c=AB\), area \(\Delta\), and angles \(A,B,C\). Let \(X\in BC\), \(Y\in CA\), \(Z\in AB\), and write \(x=BX\), \(y=CY\), \(z=AZ\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
u&=x\cos A+(c-z)\cos C,& p&=x\sin A-(c-z)\sin C,\\
v&=y\cos B+(a-x)\cos A,& q&=y\sin B-(a-x)\sin A,\\
w&=z\cos C+(b-y)\cos B,& r&=z\sin C-(b-y)\sin B.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then, with \(P(XYZ)=XY+YZ+ZX\),
\[
P(XYZ)-\frac{8\Delta^2}{abc}
=\bigl(\sqrt{u^2+p^2}-u\bigr)+\bigl(\sqrt{v^2+q^2}-v\bigr)+\bigl(\sqrt{w^2+r^2}-w\bigr).
\]
Every summand on the right is nonnegative, and equality holds exactly for the orthic triangle. If \(D=\max\{a,b,c\}\), \(x_0=c\cos B\), \(y_0=a\cos C\), and \(z_0=b\cos A\), then the exact remainder implies the global stability bounds
\[
P(XYZ)-\frac{8\Delta^2}{abc}\ge \frac{p^2+q^2+r^2}{2D}
\ge \frac{\sin^2A\,(x-x_0)^2+\sin^2B\,(y-y_0)^2+\sin^2C\,(z-z_0)^2}{2D}.
\]
scientific_limitations: The orthic minimizer and the trigonometric side decompositions are prior work; the accepted claim is the explicit exact remainder together with the global quadratic stability corollary.
The coefficient 1/(2D) in the stability inequality is not claimed to be sharp.
Older literature under different terminology may contain an equivalent remainder identity; the inspected sources and semantic searches did not reveal one.
title: Exact remainder and global quadratic stability for Fagnano's theorem
